title: Add `athena check --attribution` and a non-blocking CI job
summary: Add an attribution check that reads only the athena/records branch, never commit trailers. It walks main's first-parent commits from the first landing-intent's expected_base onward. It is exposed as `athena check --attribution`, with a non-blocking CI job on pushes to main and on schedule. The audience is the maintainer and CI, who need unrecorded commits on main named.

defaults_applied.how: Four required scenario tests plus clippy and fmt criteria.
Behavior criteria name cargo test and cargo run commands.
Criteria check pass, fail and pending outcomes, not just that the module exists.
The check is a CI job, non-blocking by design for now.
One check, one flag, one CI job.
The check is written in Rust.
The change adds no secrets or personal data.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Landing records have host_commit, intent and pr_number but no tree or base. 'Head tree equals commit tree and expected base is its parent' is judged through the linked landing-intent, using LandingIntent::matches (head_tree_sha, expected_base) in crates/athena-data/src/history.rs.

The logic goes in a new athena-core module beside pr_check.rs, with the command wired in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs as `athena check --attribution`, conflicting with --history and --pr-head. Exit 0 on pass, 2 on a finding, matching the existing checks.
The 15-minute pending window runs from the intent's created_at against an injected clock, so tests are deterministic.
A non-fast-forward in the records branch's history is reported as a finding. The check walks the records branch's first-parent chain and verifies each commit descends from the previous one.

The walk starts at the earliest landing-intent's expected_base. Commits before that base are out of scope, and with no landing-intent records at all the check says so rather than reporting a bare success.

The CI job is a new job in .github/workflows/ci.yml with continue-on-error: true. It runs on push to main and on schedule, uses the same pinned actions and setup as the history job, and runs `athena check --attribution`.

Whether the 'commit the first landing-intent record expects as its base' is itself checked is unspecified. I assume it is the exclusive starting point's first checked commit, i.e. the walk includes the commits after it. The design doc sections 5.2, 6 and 10 may settle this, and I did not read them.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: a test with a properly landed squash (landing-intent plus landing whose host_commit is the commit, tree equal to the intent's head tree, parent equal to its expected base) passes the attribution check.
Run `cargo test`: a test with a main commit that has no landing record and no matching intent makes the check fail, and the report names that commit's sha as unattributed.
Run `cargo test`: a commit with a matching landing-intent and no landing passes when the check time is within 15 minutes of the intent's created_at, and fails after 15 minutes.
Run `cargo test`: a records-branch history containing a commit that is not a fast-forward of its predecessor is reported by the check.
Run `cargo run -- check --attribution --help` or `cargo run -- check --help`: the flag is listed, and combining it with --history or --pr-head is rejected.

The check reads only records on the athena/records branch and main's first-parent commit graph. Nothing in it parses commit-message trailers, and commits before the first intent's expected_base are not judged.

.github/workflows/ci.yml has a new attribution job beside the history job. It has continue-on-error: true, runs on push to main and on schedule only, runs `athena check --attribution`, and pins actions by SHA like the existing jobs. It is not a required check.
Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean, and `cargo test` passes for the whole workspace.
The new code has doc comments citing records-history.md sections 5.2, 6 and 10 and D111. If the repo keeps a changelog entry per change, CHANGELOG.md has one.

out_of_scope: Judging commits before the first intent's expected_base (the old history check and the later legacy rule).
Making the attribution job a required check or changing branch protection (the cutover is a later job).
Part 2 of job 5 and any change to the landing or intent writers.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or setup.sh.
departures: Slightly above the reference cost. The change is a new module with git-graph and records-branch tests, a CLI flag, and a CI edit. The records-branch fast-forward test also needs fixture repositories.
